summary.text: Jason Rarick is a Republican state senator from Minnesota who represents District 11 and is seeking re-election on November 3, 2026.
He is an electrical contractor who previously served in the Minnesota House of Representatives.

paragraphs.text: Rarick graduated from Pine City High School in 1988 and received an Associate of Applied Science from Dunwoody College of Technology in Minneapolis.
He joined the St. Paul Electrical Union, IBEW 110, in 1992, became a master electrician in 1997, and in 2004 began work as a self-employed contractor at Rarick Electric.
Rarick represented District 11B in the Minnesota House of Representatives from 2015 to 2019.
He won a special general election for Minnesota State Senate District 11 on February 5, 2019, defeating Stu Lourey, and assumed office on February 13, 2019.

In the 2025-2026 session he was assigned to the Education Finance Committee, where he was ranking minority member, the Energy and Utilities Finance and Policy Committee and the Senate Higher Education Finance and Policy Committee.
In the 2026 general election he is on the ballot with Mary Carlson (D) and Monique Doward of the Forward Independence Party; the Republican primary was canceled.
